learnings.question: Which economist is famous for a 1971 observation that an information-rich world necessarily creates a scarcity of attention?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon noted in 1971 that an information-rich world creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of those who receive it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which practice is described in Hadith 12 of the 40 Hadith an-Nawawi collection as part of the perfection of a Muslim's Islam?
options: Leaving that which does not concern him
learnings.learning: Hadith 12 of the 40 Hadith an-Nawawi states that part of the perfection of one's Islam is leaving that which does not concern him.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century researcher demonstrated that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed in the 1880s that we forget roughly 80% of what we learn within 24 hours unless we actively force ourselves to recall it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What is the common term for the tendency to forget information that you know is easily searchable online, often linked to the 'Google Effect'?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call the tendency to forget easily-searchable information 'Digital Amnesia'.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact is a visual chart that tracks remaining work in a Sprint to show whether a team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart visualizes the progress of a Sprint, showing remaining work and whether the team is on schedule.

learnings.question: Which of these is commonly mistaken for an official Scrum role, even though it is NOT one of the three key roles defined by the framework?
learnings.learning: The three key roles in Scrum are Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers — Project Manager is not one of them.

learnings.question: What is the Arabic term, derived from Quran 2:30, for humanity's role as a steward or caretaker of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Quran 2:30 describes humanity's role as khalifah — a steward or caretaker of the Earth and its creation.

learnings.question: According to Quran 51:56, for what fundamental purpose did Allah state He created mankind and the jinn?
options: To multiply and populate the earth
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states Allah created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, framing worship as humanity's foundational purpose.

learnings.question: Which promise does Quran 14:7 make to those who are grateful for Allah's blessings?
options: He will forgive their past sins
He will protect them from all hardship
He will grant them Paradise immediately
He will increase them in favor
learnings.learning: Quran 14:7 promises that if people are grateful, Allah will surely increase them in favor.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power link state is meant for only very short periods of idleness and lets the link wake up almost instantly?
learnings.learning: L0s is a very light sleep state designed for short durations of idleness, allowing the PCIe link to quickly wake up and resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state is the deepest, offering the greatest power savings but requiring the longest time to resume activity — comparable to a computer being completely shut down?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, where the device is almost completely powered down, maximizing power savings at the cost of the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, as shaped by their own actions and decisions?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in life, shaped by a person's actions and decisions.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: Which statement best describes how Dua (supplication) relates to Qada' and Qadr in Islamic theology?
options: Dua has no effect, since Qada' and Qadr are both unchangeable
Dua can change a person's Qada', but that very change was already known to Allah as part of His Qadr
Qada' determines Qadr, rather than the other way around
Dua can change Qadr itself, since Qadr is not fixed
learnings.learning: Sincere Dua and actions can alter a person's Qada', but that change was always already known to Allah as part of His eternal Qadr.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: In a word-frequency analysis of the Quran's Arabic text, what percentage of the entire Quran do the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: A data analysis of the Quran's Arabic text found that the top 20 most frequent words account for only about 20.83% of the Quran, not 80% as the Pareto principle might suggest.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is the term for the diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds, similar to how vowels work in English.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
